evals.prompt: We're quietly discontinuing a subscription product next month. Do we need to tell anyone?
evals.expected_output: Should strongly push back on silent discontinuation, flagging it as the single most damaging mistake this skill names explicitly. Should require direct, proactive notice to subscription/repeat-purchase customers with enough lead time to adjust, explaining the churn and trust-damage consequences of a silent stop.
assertions: Pushes back strongly on silent discontinuation of a subscription product
Requires direct, proactive customer notice with lead time
Explains the trust/churn consequence of silence
Flags this as the skill's single most damaging named mistake

evals.prompt: We had a safety issue found in one of our products and need to pull it. What's the marketing plan?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this as the Emergency Phase-Out (recall/safety) case, distinct from a normal gradual wind-down, and defer to legal/compliance as the lead function rather than drafting recall language itself. Should recommend immediate campaign/ad pulls, coordinated PR if the story is public, and direct unambiguous customer notification with no promotional framing — and should explicitly warn against folding the disposition into routine overstock/clearance channels.
assertions: Recognizes this as the emergency/recall case, distinct from normal phase-out
Defers recall notice drafting to legal/compliance rather than authoring it
Recommends immediate pulling of live campaigns/ads
Warns against folding disposal into routine overstock/clearance channels

evals.prompt: We're launching a replacement product. The old one still has a lot of unsold inventory. Should we just go full-throttle marketing the new one right away?
evals.expected_output: Should flag the cannibalization/internal-competition risk of pushing the successor at full volume while the predecessor still has significant unsold stock. Should recommend coordinating the sell-through timeline with overstock and deciding deliberately between a hard cutover and a parallel-availability window rather than defaulting to full-throttle promotion of the new product.
assertions: Flags the risk of cannibalizing predecessor sell-through with full-throttle new promotion
Recommends coordinating with overstock on the outgoing product's timeline
Presents the hard-cutover vs. parallel-availability decision explicitly
Does not simply endorse full-throttle promotion of the successor immediately

evals.prompt: We're changing our packaging design slightly but the product formula is exactly the same. Do we need a new SKU and a big announcement?
evals.expected_output: Should recommend matching disclosure to the actual change — a packaging redesign with no functional change needs minimal explanation, not a big announcement. Should note the tradeoff of a new SKU/GTIN resetting accumulated review history and ad learning data, and recommend keeping the same SKU if the change doesn't legally or practically require a new one.
assertions: Recommends minimal disclosure for a purely cosmetic change
Explains the cost of unnecessarily resetting SKU/GTIN history
Recommends keeping the same SKU where the change doesn't require a new one
Distinguishes this from a case requiring proactive, detailed communication
